title: Place your number plates on hold/in storage
summary: You can reserve and store your number plates at a Service NSW Centre for later use.
intro: You can put your number plates in storage/on hold for later use. This means your number plates will be reserved and physically stored at a Service NSW Centre until you want to use them.
who_can_apply: The plates are currently in use on a vehicle with an active registration.
The plates were used on a vehicle whose registration expired less than 3 months ago.
The plates were ordered but are not in use yet.
The plates are lost, stolen, or destroyed plates.
The plates are attached to a vehicle with a cancelled registration.
what_you_need: The PDF form: 'Number Plates and/or Cancellation of Registration'
The number plates you want reserved.

how_to_steps.text: Download and complete the form Number Plates and/or Cancellation of Registration – PDF.
Remove the number plates from the vehicle.
Visit the service centre where you want the plates stored and submit the completed form, the plates and your payment (minimum one year).
Request general issue plates to put on your registered vehicle, or cancel your vehicle registration.
Download and complete the form Number Plates and/or Cancellation of Registration – PDF.
Visit the service centre where you want the plates stored and submit the completed form, the plates and your payment (minimum one year).

more_info.text: Both number plates must be stored, not just one. If one of the plates has been lost, stolen or destroyed, you need to report it to the NSW Police and surrender the remaining plate.
You can store your plates for a minimum of one year and up to 5 years at a time.
You’ll also have to pay the annual fee for personalised and custom number plates while they are in storage.
You'll be sent a notification letter 21 days before the storage period expires to remind you to renew, or to pick up your plates. If you don’t renew or collect, the plates will be destroyed.

faqs.q: Who can store their number plates?
faqs.a: You can store plates that are currently in use on a vehicle with an active registration, or plates that were used on a vehicle whose registration expired less than 3 months ago. Other types include trade, conditional, consular, damaged, lost, stolen, destroyed, recalled, or plates attached to a vehicle with a cancelled registration.

faqs.q: What do I need to store my number plates?
faqs.a: You need the 'Number Plates and/or Cancellation of Registration' PDF form, the number plates themselves, proof of identity, payment, and a current certificate of registration (if available).

faqs.q: How do I store my number plates?
faqs.a: You must download and complete the form, remove the plates from the vehicle, and then visit a Service NSW Centre to submit the completed form, the plates, and your payment.
